_note: One unit = one lesson path in five steps. Write 'God' (the Muslim view shows 'Allah'). Verses by ref only (shown from src/data/ayahs.json); hadith by id only (shown from src/data/hadith.json). 'about' lines are our own words, never a translation.

intro.muslim: A man passed a ruined town and wondered how God could ever bring it back to life. So God showed him: He caused him to die for a hundred years, then raised him. Watch what he saw when he woke.
intro.curious: A man passed a ruined town and wondered how it could ever be brought back to life. In the Quran's telling, God caused him to die for a hundred years, then raised him. Watch what he saw when he woke.

muslim.situation: You find a wallet with cash in it, and no one saw you pick it up.

options.label: Keep the cash and drop the wallet.
options.feedback: No one saw. Muslims believe every deed, even an atom's weight, will be seen again. The teaching explains.

options.label: Hand it in or track down the owner, cash and all.
options.feedback: That's what belief in the Last Day looks like day to day: acting as if every deed counts, because it does.

options.label: Keep a small reward and return the rest.
options.feedback: Helping yourself to part of it is still taking it. See what the Quran says about even small deeds.

options.label: Leave it where it was: not your problem.
options.feedback: At least you didn't take it. But someone has lost their money, and you could help.

curious.situation: You find a wallet with cash in it, and no one saw you pick it up.

options.label: Keep the cash and drop the wallet.
options.feedback: No one saw. Muslims believe every deed, however small, will be seen again one day.

options.label: Find the owner or hand it in, cash and all.
options.feedback: Acting as if every deed counts: that's how Muslims say belief in the Last Day should show.

options.label: Keep a little as a reward.
options.feedback: It's still taking what isn't yours. See what Islam says about small deeds.

options.label: Leave it where it was.
options.feedback: You didn't take it. But someone has lost their money, and you could help.

heading.muslim: What God teaches about the Last Day
heading.curious: What Islam teaches about the Last Day

quran.about: The man is caused to die for a hundred years and raised; his food is unspoiled, and he watches his donkey brought back to life, bone by bone.
Someone asks who will give life to bones once they have crumbled; the answer: the One who made them the first time.
The Hour is coming, there is no doubt of it, and God will raise those in the graves.
Whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it.

hadith.about: Belief in the Last Day is one of the six pillars of faith.
Believing in the Last Day shows in how you speak and how you treat neighbours and guests.

insights.text: Muslims believe this life will end, every person will be raised, and everyone will see what they did, down to an atom's weight (99:7-8). Only God knows when, and only He judges anyone's end.
The Prophet ﷺ tied belief in the Last Day to everyday things: saying good or staying silent, and honouring neighbours and guests (Bukhari 6018). Belief in the Last Day is meant to change today.

check.q: What did the man wonder as he passed the ruined town?
options: How God would bring it back to life after its death
check.why: He wondered how God would ever bring the town back to life after its death (2:259).

check.q: How long did the man stay dead?
check.why: God caused him to die for a hundred years, then raised him.

check.q: What did he see happen to his donkey?
options: It was brought back to life before his eyes
check.why: He watched his donkey brought back to life.

check.q: Who will give life to crumbled bones, according to 36:79?
options: The One who made them the first time
check.why: The One who created them the first time will give them life again.

check.q: What does 99:7-8 teach about small deeds?
options: Even an atom's weight of good or evil will be seen
They are forgotten after a year
check.why: Whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and likewise evil.

reflection.muslim: If you knew today's smallest kindness would be shown to you again one day, what kindness would you do today?
reflection.curious: Does believing that every deed matters change how you'd live? Which of your small habits would you want to see again?
